neighbours.label: the comparison operator word: the verb 'compare' (active, present) or 'between' directly after a resemblance noun (resemblance, similarity, parallel)
fire: Critics often compare her early novels with those of Woolf.
The teacher asked the class to compare the two translations line by line.
Visitors remarked on the resemblance between the twins and their grandfather.
It is tempting to compare the brain to a computer, but the analogy breaks down.
Biologists have long noticed the similarity between bat wings and human hands.
Before buying, compare the warranties offered by each manufacturer.
The report draws a parallel between the two financial crises.
You cannot compare a wooden boat with a steel hull on strength alone.
quiet: Critics often praise her early novels and ignore the later ones.
The teacher asked the class to read the two translations aloud.
Visitors remarked on the warmth between the twins and their grandfather.
It is tempting to ignore the brain's complexity, but the simplification fails.
Biologists have long studied the bones between the wrist and the fingers.
Before buying, read the warranties offered by each manufacturer.
The report describes the decade between the two financial crises.
A wooden boat was moored beside the steel hull all winter.
